questions.q: def add_tax(price, rate=0.08) is called as add_tax(50). What value does rate have inside the function?
options: An error is raised because rate is missing
questions.explain: A parameter with a default value uses that default when the caller does not supply the argument.

questions.q: A function computes x * 2 in its body but has no return statement. What does calling it give back?
questions.explain: Without return, a function returns None. The computed value is discarded.

questions.q: With totals = [20.0, 55.5, 130.0, 8.25], what does [t for t in totals if t > 20] produce?
questions.explain: The trailing if filters: only totals greater than 20 are kept, giving [55.5, 130.0].

questions.q: What is the difference between an if at the end of a comprehension and an if ... else at the front?
options: The trailing if filters items out; the leading if ... else chooses a value for every item
The trailing if is faster but produces the same result
The leading if ... else filters items and the trailing if transforms them
questions.explain: A trailing if drops items that fail the test. A leading if ... else picks between two values for each item, so the output length is unchanged.

questions.q: What does sorted(orders, key=lambda o: o[1], reverse=True) do for a list of (name, amount) pairs?
questions.explain: The lambda picks the second element (the amount) as the sort key, and reverse=True puts the largest first.
